1 # Offline campaign compiler and replay certificate, version 3.0
   2 
   3 The project is a multi-file typed model toolkit. Complete its offline pipeline:
   4 layout compilation, symbolic-test recovery, scoped input validation, canonical
   5 corpus assembly, and stateful test preparation. Run `python3 project/campaign_cli.py`.
   6 Its JSON certificate is the graded interface; implementation organization is free.
   7 The supplied AST/type visitor/graph APIs are useful editable project components.
   8 This profile consumes recorded symbolic objects. It does not synthesize models,
   9 execute generated C, invoke a symbolic engine, contact servers, or infer bugs from
  10 model-return values. State machines and predicate semantics below are explicit inputs.
  11 
  12 ## Framing and domain
  13 
  14 stdin is one UTF-8 JSON object, at most 64 MiB including whitespace. Duplicate
  15 object keys, nonfinite numbers, invalid UTF-8, malformed JSON, and trailing JSON
  16 produce exactly `{"error":"INVALID_INPUT"}` and exit zero. Otherwise configurations
  17 obey all schemas, references, types, acyclicity conditions, and coupled bounds in
  18 this document. Out-of-domain configuration validation is not required. Recorded
  19 KTEST payloads may be arbitrary, including malformed data, and are handled per run.
  20 Output is exactly one JSON object and exit zero; diagnostics use stderr.
  21 
  22 The root has `types`, `modules`, `calls`, `pipes`, `entries`, `machine`, `runs`.
  23 All lists preserve their given order unless another order is specified. Identifiers
  24 are ASCII `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*`, at most 32 characters, and unique in their scope.
  25 Names in separate scopes may coincide. JSON object ordering is immaterial.
  26 
  27 `types` is a list of named definitions with `name`, `kind`, and these extra fields:
  28 
  29 | kind | extra fields | value |
  30 | --- | --- | --- |
  31 | bool | none | Boolean |
  32 | char | none | one Latin-1 character, including NUL |
  33 | int | `bits`: 1..64 | unsigned integer in [0,2^bits) |
  34 | string | `maxsize`: 0..512 | bounded Latin-1 C string |
  35 | enum | `values`: distinct nonempty strings | one listed string |
  36 | array | `element`: type name, `size`: 0..4096 | ordered fixed-length list |
  37 | struct | `fields`: ordered `[field_name,type_name]` pairs | object with exactly these fields |
  38 | alias | `target`: type name | transparent value/layout alias |
  39 | void | none | no value, only permitted directly as a module result |
  40 
  41 Forward references and shared subtypes are allowed; the type graph is acyclic.
  42 Aliases are transparent to expressions and values but retain their declaration name.
  43 Strings recover bytes before the first NUL, or all maxsize bytes if none is NUL;
  44 all maxsize bytes still belong to the symbolic inventory. String(0) recovers `""`.
  45 Enum strings and state/command names are nonempty printable ASCII, at most 64 chars.
  46 Struct field names are unique. No aggregate contains void. Type nesting depth is
  47 at most 64. A result array/struct is a by-value symbolic result in this profile.
  48 
  49 A module has `name`, `params` (ordered `[parameter_name,type_name]` pairs),
  50 `result` (`[result_name,type_name]`), and `requires` (a predicate or null meaning true).
  51 Parameter/result names are distinct. An entry's result may be void. Filters have a
  52 Boolean result, although their acceptance comes from their `requires` predicate.
  53 `calls` contains `[caller,callee]` dependencies; duplicate pairs have no extra effect.
  54 A pipe is `{"target":module,"filter":module,"bind":{filter_parameter:target_parameter,...}}`.
  55 Every filter parameter is bound once to a compatible underlying target parameter type.
  56 Pipes are local to their target. A filter's own pipes apply transitively using the
  57 composed bindings. Their acceptance is its own predicate AND its bound filters'
  58 acceptance. Reusing a filter with different bindings means different applications.
  59 Call dependencies affect compilation, not execution of predicates on missing helper
  60 arguments. All call and pipe dependency edges together form a DAG.
  61 `entries` lists distinct module names, in required plan order.
  62 
  63 ## Predicate language
  64 
  65 Predicates are typed expression arrays. Configurations are well typed. A variable
  66 refers to a module input, or the nearest enclosing `all` binding. Results are not
  67 predicate inputs. `const` values obey the given type's JSON value representation.
  68 In particular, a string constant is a literal Latin-1 JSON string of length
  69 0..maxsize, including any embedded NUL characters. No truncation or padding is
  70 applied to constants, including strings nested inside aggregate constants.
  71 For String(3), `"a\u0000b"` is a valid three-character constant, distinct from
  72 `"a"`; a recovered symbolic byte sequence a,NUL,b has the value `"a"`.
  73 String(0) permits only the empty constant. NUL truncation applies only when
  74 recovering symbolic string objects, not to expression values or equality.
  75 
  76 | form | meaning |
  77 | --- | --- |
  78 | `["var",name]` | lexical variable |
  79 | `["const",type_name,value]` | typed constant |
  80 | `["field",value,field_name]` | struct field |
  81 | `["index",array,index]` | fixed valid zero-based index |
  82 | `["all",binding,array,predicate]` | every element satisfies predicate, binding that element |
  83 | `["match",string,pattern]` | full byte-string regular-language membership |
  84 | `["not",predicate]` | Boolean complement |
  85 | `[op,left,right]` | binary operation |
  86 
  87 Binary operations: `eq`, `ne` compare same-underlying-type values deeply; `lt`,
  88 `le`, `gt`, `ge` compare unsigned integers; `add`, `sub` use modulo 2^bits of
  89 that integer type; `and`, `or`, `implies` are Boolean with left-to-right short
  90 circuiting. `all` over an empty array is true. Binding shadowing is lexical and
  91 must not affect enclosing/sibling predicates. Array indexing is statically valid.
  92 
  93 Patterns contain printable ASCII. Grammar: union of sequences with `|`, sequence
  94 of zero or more atoms, and zero or more postfix `*` repetitions on an atom. Atoms
  95 are a literal, `(union)`, or a nonempty character class `[items]`. An item is a
  96 literal or ascending `low-high` range. Backslash escapes the next character both
  97 inside and outside classes. Unescaped `()[]|*\` are grammar symbols outside
  98 classes; `-`, `]`, `\` must be escaped when used literally inside a class.
  99 Other characters, including `.`, are literal. Empty pattern, empty sequence,
 100 empty union alternatives, and repetition of nullable expressions are supported.
 101 No anchors, dot wildcard, `+`, `?`, negated classes, or numeric escapes exist.
 102 Matching is over Latin-1 code points with ASCII ranges; all other byte values
 103 fail ranges that exclude them. Precedence is repetition, sequence, then union.
 104 
 105 ## Compilation certificate and symbolic wire identity
 106 
 107 For each entry produce one plan with exactly `entry`, `modules`, `types`, `slots`,
 108 `flag`, `variables`. `modules` is the root plus all transitive call/pipe prerequisites,
 109 ordered so prerequisites precede dependents; among currently eligible modules use
 110 lexicographically smallest name. Unrelated modules/filters are absent.
 111 `types` lists enum, struct, and alias declaration names reachable from these
 112 modules' params/results: dependency-before-user postorder, each declaration once,
 113 first encounters following module order, parameter order then result, struct field
 114 order, and array/alias child order. Primitive/array/string definition names are
 115 not C declaration names and do not appear in this list.
 116 
 117 `slots` is an ordered list of `[object_name,path,byte_width]`. `path` begins with
 118 an entry parameter/result name, followed by field names and zero-based indices.
 119 It describes the entry's own symbolic harness, independent of helper signatures.
 120 The exact numbering contract follows the toolkit's `MainBuilder` convention:
 121 inputs in parameter order, then non-void result, start at x0; each visited bool,
 122 char, int, enum, string buffer, array, or struct reserves one increasing xN.
 123 A scalar has one object; a composite itself has no object, then its children in
 124 order reserve IDs recursively. String(N) has N character objects after its buffer
 125 ID, not one packed object. Alias reserves no ID and adds no path component.
 126 Even zero-length composites reserve their own ID. Void reserves none.
 127 Widths: bool/char 1; int the smallest of 1,2,4,8 bytes holding its bits; enum 4.
 128 Scalar object order is harness order, independent of KTEST object ordering.
 129 If the entry has at least one direct pipe, one final scalar Boolean object is
 130 reserved for `bad_input`; `flag` is its xN name, and it is not in `slots`.
 131 Otherwise `flag` is null. `variables` is the total reserved ID count, including
 132 non-object composites and any flag. An unused helper/filter consumes no entry IDs.
 133 
 134 Each run has `entry` (one of entries) and `ktest` (standard base64 string, without
 135 whitespace). Decoded binary KTEST v3 layout: ASCII `KTEST`, big-endian uint32
 136 version=3, uint32 argument_count, then that many blobs; uint32 symbolic_argv_count
 137 and uint32 symbolic_argv_length; uint32 object_count; then object name blob/data
 138 blob pairs. Every blob is a uint32 byte length followed by exactly that many bytes.
 139 Arguments are opaque and ignored (at most 64 arguments, each at most 256 bytes).
 140 Symbolic-argv bookkeeping values are ignored. No trailing byte is allowed.
 141 An object name is canonical ASCII `x` plus a nonnegative decimal integer with no
 142 leading zeros. Every expected slot/flag occurs exactly once with exactly its width;
 143 unknown or duplicate objects, including composite IDs, invalidate the test.
 144 Object order is arbitrary. Leaf values are little-endian unsigned integers:
 145 bool and flag must be 0/1, chars 0..255, ints must have all padding bits zero,
 146 and enum indices must be in range. Strings consume all character objects even
 147 after a NUL. Missing objects cannot be repaired by skipping to a nearby xN.
 148 Any base64/binary/inventory/leaf-range error makes just that run INVALID_TEST.
 149 
 150 The flag attests to pipe acceptance only: it must equal NOT(all the entry's
 151 bound filters accept, transitively). A mismatch is INVALID_TEST, even if another
 152 predicate would reject that run. Once this attestation is consistent, a false
 153 entry predicate or false bound filter makes the run FILTERED. Results from the
 154 recorded model never establish whether an implementation has a bug.
 155 
 156 ## Stateful preparation and corpus identity
 157 
 158 `machine` is null for stateless campaigns. Otherwise it has `states`, `initial`,
 159 `state_param`, `message_param`, and `transitions`. Every entry has those input
 160 parameters: state is an enum over these states and message is a string.
 161 A transition has `from`, `to`, `command`, `cost` (integer 1..65535), and `when`
 162 (predicate or null). `(from,command)` pairs are unique. Its predicate is evaluated
 163 on the recovered entry inputs, including the desired state, not an intermediate
 164 simulation state. These guards are well typed for every entry. Transitions may
 165 form cycles. Records and their preambles start from initial independently.
 166 
 167 A usable preparation is a path of enabled transitions from initial to the
 168 recovered desired state. Minimize `(sum of costs, number of commands, command
 169 sequence lexicographically)` exactly. These supplied costs model replay setup
 170 bytes/work; this is not a hardware timing objective. If no usable path exists,
 171 mark the record UNREACHABLE. Otherwise append the recovered message to its
 172 preparation commands. Corpus `cost` includes preparation only. For stateless
 173 campaigns commands=[] and cost=0. The initial state needs no preparation.
 174 
 175 A corpus identity is `(entry, recovered input values)`, excluding model result,
 176 raw bytes after a string NUL, transport arguments, object order, and preparation
 177 metadata. Arrays/objects/booleans/integers retain their JSON type identity; empty
 178 arrays and empty objects differ. Never merge different entries. Assign corpus
 179 indices by first usable run order; keep every usable witness run index in order.
 180 
 181 Output has exactly `plans`, `records`, `corpus`. Plans follow entries order;
 182 records follow runs order. Each record is one of:
 183 
 184 * `{"status":"INVALID_TEST"}`, `{"status":"FILTERED"}`, or `{"status":"UNREACHABLE"}`;
 185 * `{"status":"READY","case":index,"model_result":value}` for a new corpus input;
 186 * same fields with status DUPLICATE for a later usable witness (even if its
 187   model result differs). Void model_result is null.
 188 
 189 A corpus entry has exactly `entry`, `inputs` (parameter-name object), `cost`,
 190 `commands`, `witnesses`. Invalid/filtered/unreachable runs never allocate corpus
 191 indices. Transport/leaf/flag errors take precedence over FILTERED; filtering
 192 precedes reachability; reachability precedes deduplication.
 193 
 194 ## Scale, development, and execution
 195 
 196 One campaign represents a collected model-testing job, with shared types and
 197 many symbolic witnesses; expanding every shared dependency path or recompiling
 198 for every witness is not part of the objective. Bounds: 8192 type definitions,
 199 4096 modules, 32 entries, 16384 calls+pipes, 16 params/module, 16 fields/struct,
 200 4096 enum values, 64 type depth, 64 expression depth, 128 characters/pattern.
 201 Across all entry plans at most 32768 scalar slots and 65536 reserved IDs;
 202 across all runs at most 2,097,152 expected objects and 4,194,304 total
 203 reserved-ID visits (sum of the corresponding plan.variables). Across usable
 204 runs, preparation commands plus final messages total at most 16,777,216 Latin-1
 205 characters, counted before corpus deduplication. These coupled replay-batch
 206 bounds also cover empty aggregates and long state preambles. Predicate source expansion is also bounded per campaign:
 207 4,194,304 expression-node instances and 8,388,608 match-byte units. For these
 208 input-size guarantees, each operator/leaf is one node, an all-body is counted
 209 once per declared array element, and a match contributes pattern-length times
 210 (1 + its string type's maxsize). Count all branches conservatively. Sum the
 211 entry predicate and every composed filter application plus distinct transition
 212 guard ASTs, for each run. Identical transition guard ASTs count once per entry
 213 per run; other applications count separately. These guarantees bound replay
 214 work even for constant/nested predicates; no counters are required in output. At most 2048 runs, 4096
 215 states, 16384 transitions, and 4096 composed pipe applications/entry. Preparation
 216 may require thousands of commands; there is no additional hop cutoff. Coupled
 217 bounds and the 64 MiB input limit all apply. Exact uint64 values remain integers.
 218 
 219 Submit the full `/workspace/project` tree, at most 8 MiB and 256 entries (files
 220 plus directories). All regular auxiliary files/directories are allowed and
 221 collected; symlinks, hard links, devices, sockets, and FIFOs are forbidden.
 222 No extension/name whitelist or extra-file rejection applies. The evaluator
 223 freezes this tree and invokes `python3 -I -B project/campaign_cli.py`. Only this
 224 project is submitted. Do not depend on sibling docs/checker, absolute host paths,
 225 network packages, installed editable packages, or verifier files. The CLI's
 226 bootstrap adds its local src/; no pip installation is needed.
 227 
 228 Ordinary nonroot development commands, with all dependencies already present:
 229 
 230 ```
 231 python3 /workspace/project/campaign_cli.py < /workspace/examples/smoke.input.json
 232 python3 /workspace/public_check.py /workspace/project
 233 ```
 234 
 235 The public checker runs real bounded children through normal stdin/stdout pipes.
 236 Text, .buffer, fd0/1, fileno, fdopen, and explicitly flushed output before
 237 os._exit(0) work. Empty/non-JSON/wrong/nonzero outputs fail. It is a sanity runner,
 238 not a security boundary; direct root execution is refused. Public fixtures cover
 239 only elementary layout and corpus identity, not the whole domain or maximum scale.
 240 The nonroot public supervisor requires the development overlay documented in
 241 WORKER-PROFILE.md; it restores the scored signal/group denials in each child.
 242 Cleanup of the child's group and adopted descendants precedes acceptance on
 243 normal and abnormal exits. Each fixture retains its120s deadline, plus at most5s
 244 for cleanup; an enclosing controller allows300s for the two-fixture command.
 245 
 246 Whole-campaign wall budget is 120s, motivated by offline campaign ingestion and
 247 state-preparation latency. Local limits are 2 GiB address space/process,
 248 180/181s soft/hard CPU per process, 64 processes/threads per leased UID, 256 FDs,
 249 64 MiB/file, initial stack soft 8 MiB/hard unlimited, core dumps zero; stdout
 250 512 MiB, stderr 1 MiB. No task sets CPU affinity. Formal requests 2 CPUs, 2 GiB
 251 memory, no GPU. Runtime CPython 3.11.14, C locale, BLAS/OMP/MKL threads 1.
 252 Python -I ignores PYTHON* environment settings; ordinary pipe buffering applies.
 253 
 254 Scored execution uses immutable runtime/project in a nonprivileged chroot;
 255 only /workspace/tmp is writable, cleared per invocation (use TMPDIR). /proc and
 256 host/private task paths are absent. The complete syscall restrictions are in
 257 WORKER-PROFILE.md; sockets/network, namespace/privilege changes, and listed
 258 IPC/process-access syscalls are denied. Ordinary subprocesses/threads are allowed
 259 within limits. Sampled scratch above 1 GiB regular-file size/allocated bytes or
 260 50000 entries aborts as infrastructure error, not a hard storage quota or score.
